claim.why_it_matters: Two index entries merged on one line. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of printed page 906 (PDF p930), left column under heading C, shows two separate top-level index entries on consecutive lines: 'Calendar date format 629' and 'CALL statement 471'. page-930.md line 26 holds both as one source line, 'Calendar date format 629 CALL statement 471', with no hard break, while every other entry on the page ends with a backslash line break. So the transcription really does fuse two distinct headwords into one entry. Both page numbers survive in order, so the text is complete, but the entry structure is wrong. The defect is structural and sits in informative matter (the index).
verdict.corrected_description: Index (printed p.906, PDF p930): the separate top-level entries 'Calendar date format 629' and 'CALL statement 471' are fused into one markdown line with no hard line break. Both page numbers are present and in the right order, so no reference is lost. The problem is that two headwords read as a single entry. The fix is to split them into two lines, with the backslash break used everywhere else on the page.
